title: [claude draft] The Golden Spike (1869)
note: Claude draft, not Nandu's final script. Narration is exactly as drafted. Tags are Claude's own tagging, so the score tests the tagging, not the script. Historical facts are not yet checked against sources.
logline: Two railroads meet in Utah; the famous photo leaves out the Chinese workers who built the western line.
narration: May tenth, eighteen sixty-nine. A desert in Utah. Two railroads, built toward each other for six years, finally meet. One from the west. One from the east. Two steam engines stop nose to nose. A crowd gathers. A golden spike waits for its hole. A railroad boss lifts the hammer. He swings. He misses. He hits the rail. The telegraph man taps out one word anyway: done. Bells ring in cities across America. A trip that took months by wagon now takes days. But look at the famous photo. Thousands of Chinese workers built the western line, through mountains, in winter. Almost none are in the picture. The golden spike was taken out that same day and replaced with an iron one. The glory was gold. The work was iron.
